key_findings.progenitor_replant_displacement: At 10 N, 156±19 μm in treated replants vs 141±23 μm WT; at 15 N, 300±26 μm vs 297±34 μm, in one rat replantation study.

interpretation: Strength, extensibility, toughness, physiologic mobility, fiber insertion and absence of ankylosis are separate restoration outcomes.
An apparent stiffness match is insufficient: parallel PDL and bone-bridge load paths can produce the same initial stiffness while differing in mobility, dissipation and tissue identity.
The evidence demonstrates animal proof-of-concept for complete progenitor-driven periodontal reattachment after replantation, not a therapy for crooked in-situ human teeth after blunt trauma.

An in-situ tooth displaced by trauma may heal in a shifted position; restoration research must measure position, socket/cementum/PDL insertion, occlusion, mobility, toughness and relapse after temporary stabilization is removed.

model_scope.name: parallel-load-path identifiability demonstration
model_scope.units: dimensionless fractions of a hypothetical control tangent stiffness
model_scope.status: illustrative algebra only; not fitted to these studies and not a finite-element or tissue constitutive model
model_scope.purpose: Show why recovered apparent stiffness alone cannot distinguish a functional shock-absorbing ligament from a stiff ankylotic bridge. Independent mobility, toughness, attachment histology and bridge measurements are needed.
